messages:
carlos (acme-cust): Hey team — we're seeing a sudden spike of 429s starting ~2025-11-02T14:02Z. Mostly hitting /v1/generate. Some traffic that should've stayed in eu-west is being routed to us-west and getting throttled. Example request ids: acm-7f1, acm-7f2, acm-7f5. Sample curl + response we got:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_acme_xxx\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-open-8b\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{\"error\":{\"code\":429,\"message\":\"rate limit exceeded\",\"request_id\":\"acm-7f1\"}}
```
Can you confirm whether this is a routing/failover issue or a quota auth problem on our end? We're seeing customer-facing latency spike too.

lina (support): Sorry about that — digging in now. Can you paste your org id and one full request-id header from the failing response (the x-request-id or request_id in body)? Also, can you try one quick repro with an explicit region header for me: add header `X-Prefer-Region: eu-west` and post the response body.

carlos (acme-cust): Org id: org-acme-88. From the body above request_id=acm-7f1. Repro with region header coming up.

raj (eng-sre): Adding some context — when a region runs out of burst credits or hits its soft capacity, the router will failover to another region by design (to preserve availability). If eu-west was short, we would fan out/redirect to us-west or us-east. That can cause unexpected 429s if target region is saturated.

raj (eng-sre): Quick checks for the support team: run this on routing logs (we have grep alias rg):
```
rg \"request_id=acm-7f1|acm-7f2|acm-7f5\" /var/log/routing/* | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Look for lines with `action=fallback` or `route=eu-west -> us-west`. Also check `x-region-route` headers in responses.

deploy-bot: Autoscaler: eu-west pool increased from 12 -> 18 GPUs at 2025-11-02T14:03:21 (trigger: burst_utilization & queue_latency).

marta (eng-platform): Noted. Short-term mitigations: 1) Enable strict_affinity for org-acme-88 (will prefer pinned region, but may increase errors if capacity is truly depleted). 2) Grant a temporary per-org burst_credits bump and token quota increase while we investigate. I can apply the bump if support approves.

lina (support): Carlos — can we try your repro now with the pref region header? If that consistently succeeds we can do the temporary quota bump and enable strict_affinity for your org. Also please include the full raw response headers (so we can confirm router decision headers: `X-Route-Trace`, `X-Serve-Region`, `X-Fallback-Reason`).

carlos (acme-cust): Ran two tests:
1) With `X-Prefer-Region: eu-west` -> HTTP/1.1 200, body OK, x-serve-region: eu-west, x-route-trace: primary.
2) No region header -> intermittently 429, one response header set: x-serve-region: us-west, x-fallback-reason: capacity_exhausted, x-request-id: acm-7f5.
So looks like failover path is kicking in and hitting us-west throttle.

raj (eng-sre): That matches the logs I pulled: snippet: 
```
[2025-11-02T14:02:58Z] request_id=acm-7f5 action=fallback from=eu-west to=us-west reason=burst_credit_exhausted
[2025-11-02T14:03:05Z] request_id=acm-7f5 response=429 to=client route=us-west queue_ms=212
```
We also have a scheduled maintenance earlier that reduced effective eu-west capacity for 20m which explains the temporary deficit.

marta (eng-platform): Filing capacity incident and temporary config now. Creating ticket INC-20251102-741 for eu-west capacity perturbation. Applying a +30% burst_credits bump and enabling strict_affinity for org-acme-88 for 2 hours.

deploy-bot: Config update: org org-acme-88 set strict_affinity=true (applied by marta).

marta (eng-platform): Applied temporary quota bump: burst_credits:+30%, token_quota:+20% for org-acme-88 until 2025-11-02T16:10Z. I also scheduled a follow-up to revert if not needed.

lina (support): Carlos, can you re-run a 1-min burst test (50 rapid requests) without the prefer-region header and confirm behavior?

carlos (acme-cust): Re-ran 50 requests at 14:07Z: 49/50 200 OK, 1/50 429. Much better. Latency back to normal. Thanks. :thumbsup:

lina (support): Great — keeping this thread open while we watch. Raj/Marta: please keep me posted if eu-west queues/burst credits drain again or if we need more permanent capacity.

raj (eng-sre): Will monitor the routing histogram and queue latencies. If we see repeated cross-region fallbacks for multiple customers I'll propose increasing eu-west steady capacity or enabling a per-org dedicated reservation.

marta (eng-platform): Follow-up: maintenance window note appended to INC-20251102-741. Root cause: rolling infra patch reduced node pool by ~25% for 12m. I'll include mitigation plan in the incident.

carlos (acme-cust): Appreciate the fast help — will ping if anything else pops.

lina (support): Marking this as resolved for customer-facing impact; we will leave incident open for platform follow-up. :white_check_mark:
